raw_case_text:
A 34-year-old male patient, from the state of Chanchamayo, Junin, Peru, with a medical history of chronic foot ulcer, was evaluated for one year with daily mucoid bloody diarrhea associated with intermittent infection by Strongyloides stercoralis, odynophagia, an ulcer in the upper palate and 12 kilogram weight loss. Over the last three months diarrhea episodes increased, and he presented with a nose ulcer. He denied chronic corticoid use, high-risk sexual behavior and had not been treated with immunosuppressive medications. Physical examination revealed a wasted patient with pale skin and upper palate, nose, mouth, and right foot ulcers (Figure 1). Blood testing showed anemia (hemoglobin 11 g/L) and hypoalbuminemia (albumin 16 g/L). He had more than 100 leucocytes and 30 red blood cells per field at the stool examination. The remaining of blood tests was normal. Parasitological studies were negatives. Chest X-ray was normal, and blood Elisa-HIV was negative. Qualitative assessment for HTLV-1 was positive. 
Colonoscopy revealed multiple deep and large patchy exudative ulcers from rectum to cecum alternating with areas of normal mucosa (Figure 2). Direct microscopic examination revealed several double wall fungi with multiple gemmulation compatible with paracoccidioidomycosis (Figure 3). 
Histopathology demonstrated acute infectious colitis with multiple granulomas rich in epithelioid cells and oval budding yeast cells consistent with Histoplasma capsulatum (Figure 4). In addition Paracoccidioides was found at a different site (Figure 5). Palate, nose, foot ulcer, sputum, and urine samples were positive for Paracoccidioides. Urine culture was positive for both Histoplasma capsulatum and Paracoccidioides brasiliensis. Blood cultures were negative for both fungi. The diagnosis of chronic progressive disseminated fungal coinfection was made. The patient received iv amphotericin B for 4 weeks as initial treatment with good response, and then he was discharged with oral itraconazole. He did not receive any treatment for HTLV-1 infections because he did not develop any mayor complications such as myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP) or adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 34-year-old male from Peru presented with a 1-year history of daily mucoid bloody diarrhea, odynophagia, an upper palatal ulcer, and 12-kg weight loss, with worsening diarrhea and a nasal ulcer over the preceding 3 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, from Chanchamayo, Junin, Peru, had a 1-year history of chronic foot ulcer, daily mucoid bloody diarrhea associated with intermittent Strongyloides stercoralis infection, odynophagia, an upper palate ulcer, and 12-kg weight loss. Over the 3 months prior to evaluation, his diarrhea frequency increased and he developed a nasal ulcer.
subjective.past_medical_history: Chronic right foot ulcer and intermittent Strongyloides stercoralis infection. Epidemiological/social history: From Chanchamayo, Junin, Peru; denied chronic corticosteroid or immunosuppressant use and denied high-risk sexual behavior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for daily mucoid bloody diarrhea, odynophagia, 12-kg weight loss, and oral, nasal, and foot ulcers.

objective.physical_examination: General: wasted appearance with pale skin. Skin/Mucosa: ulcers on the upper palate, nose, mouth, and right foot.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs: Hb 11 g/dL, albumin 16 g/L, remaining blood tests normal; HIV ELISA negative. Stool exam: >100 leukocytes and 30 RBCs per field; parasitological studies negative. Chest X-ray: normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Virology: qualitative HTLV-1 assay positive. Colonoscopy: multiple deep, large patchy exudative ulcers from the rectum to the cecum alternating with normal mucosa. Direct microscopy & histopathology: colonic biopsy showed acute infectious colitis with epithelioid granulomas containing oval budding yeast cells consistent with Histoplasma capsulatum, plus double-walled multi-budding yeasts of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis at a separate colonic site and in palate, nose, foot ulcer, sputum, and urine samples.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Chronic progressive disseminated Histoplasma capsulatum and Paracoccidioides brasiliensis coinfection associated with underlying HTLV-1 infection. Confirmation: Colonic histopathology and direct microscopy showing both H. capsulatum and P. brasiliensis, and urine fungal culture positive for both Histoplasma capsulatum and Paracoccidioides brasiliensis (blood cultures negative). Plan & clinical course: Treated with IV amphotericin B for 4 weeks with good clinical response, then discharged on oral itraconazole (no specific therapy required for asymptomatic HTLV-1 carrier state).
